chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who says 'La la'mari' while he is in ihram. He said: 'It is not al-jidal (oath-swearing). Rather, al-jidal is when a man says 'La wallahi' and 'Bala wallahi'. As for his saying 'La ha', it is merely seeking the name (of the oath). And his saying 'Ya hanah' is no problem. As for his saying 'La bali shani'aka', then it is from the speech of al-jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance).'
The Sheikh (peace be upon him) said: And whoever removes a louse from his skin and kills it or throws it away, let him feed a handful of food in its place.

key_terms.مُحْرِم: One in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for oaths and killing lice while in ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to clarify the distinction between binding oaths (jidal) and casual exclamations for those in ihram, emphasizing that phrases like 'la amri' do not incur penalty unless they constitute a serious oath. The hadith further extends the principle of minor expiation (kaffarah) to the accidental killing or discarding of a louse, requiring a measure of food (kaffarat al-dam) as a practical application of ritual purity laws.
